const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/gauntlet/critics/nav-chrome-r2.md
+## Verdict
+- piece: nav-chrome
+- round: r2
+- winner: bar
+- biggest_gap: R2 is cleaner and more usable, but still looks like a default product header: full-width rule, cyan circular mark, three links, amber underline, and boxed theme icon. Rail geometry removes the pill; it does not create authorship. Bar references either own a mark/structural frame (dai, eftakher), carry a distinctive surface (pham), or delete nav with confidence (evilrabbit, logan, pablo). Ours is quiet, not memorable.
+- next_build_instruction: Keep full-width rail, exact route labels, active underline, and 32px theme control. Add one unmistakable brand-specific rail signature that survives 390px: an authored mark/wordmark lockup or structural offset/rule system with deliberate spacing, not another capsule. Make the signature do the identity work; do not add more controls, glow, or decoration. Recapture dark/light desktop/mobile and judge nav-cropped identity again.
+- evidence_paths:
+  - gauntlet/pieces/nav-chrome/r2/header-desktop.png
+  - gauntlet/pieces/nav-chrome/r2/header-mobile.png
+  - gauntlet/pieces/nav-chrome/r2/header-desktop-light.png

+  - gauntlet/bar/WIN_CRITERIA.md
+  - gauntlet/bar/INDEX.md
+  - gauntlet/bar/NOTES.md
+  - gauntlet/bar/dai-is-a-dev/nav-desktop.png

+- blind_ab_note: Picked before label reveal. Unlabeled A = r2 desktop/mobile dark+light rail and toggle crops; unlabeled B = bar nav desktop/mobile set. A wins clarity, route legibility, active-state visibility, and theme affordance. B wins authored identity, compositional confidence, and template resistance. B wins overall because this crop is judged as chrome, not merely functional navigation; several B sites intentionally omit nav, which is stronger than generic chrome.
*** End Patch";
